Zillow (CIK 1617640), XBRL, $M. FCF = CFO - capex:
FY2023: 354 - 135 = 219; revenue 1,945 -> 11.3%
FY2024: 428 - 143 = 285; revenue 2,236 -> 12.7%
FY2025: 368 - 133 = 235; revenue 2,583 -> 9.1%

Trend: not a clean trend. FCF margin improved ~140bps in 2024, then fell ~365bps in 2025. Absolute FCF is roughly flat ($219m -> $285m -> $235m) while revenue grew 33% over the period, so margin is compressing as CFO fails to keep pace with revenue growth. Capex is stable at ~$133-143m (5-7% of revenue).

United States Steel (CIK 1163302; ticker X delisted after the Nippon Steel deal, reached via CIK). FY2024 XBRL:
Cost of goods and services sold: $14,060m
Inventory, net: 12/31/2023 $2,128m; 12/31/2024 $2,168m; average $2,148m

Inventory turnover = 14,060 / 2,148 = 6.55x (about 56 days of inventory).
On an ending-inventory basis: 14,060 / 2,168 = 6.49x.

For context, FY2023 turnover was 15,803 / ((2,359+2,128)/2 = 2,243.5) = 7.04x, so turnover slowed in 2024 as COGS fell 11% while inventory was flat.

Take rate = revenue / GBV (GBV from 10-K MD&A key business metrics; revenue from XBRL):
FY2022: $8,399m / $63,212m = 13.29%
FY2023: $9,917m / $73,252m = 13.54%
FY2024: $11,102m / $81,784m = 13.57%

Trend: modestly rising and then flattening. +25bps in 2023, only +3bps in 2024. Over three years take rate expanded ~28bps, i.e. revenue grew slightly faster than GBV (revenue +32% vs GBV +29% 2022-2024). Effectively a stable ~13.3-13.6% monetisation rate rather than meaningful take-rate expansion.

Yes. Workday historically disclosed BOTH in MD&A of its 10-K/10-Q: "gross and net revenue retention rates exceeding 95% and 100%, respectively" (e.g. 10-Q for Q2 FY2025). After SEC comment letters, Workday stated (CORRESP 9/19/2024) it would stop disclosing net revenue retention and would disclose the actual then-current gross rate.

Current definition (FY2026 10-K, filed 3/6/2026): gross revenue retention rate ~97% as of 1/31/2026 - "measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers... calculated by taking total annual recurring revenue (ARR) of our customers as of the corresponding prior period-end and comparing it to ARR for the current period from that same set of customers." It captures churn but excludes add-ons/net expansion (volume and price).
